label: copy-phase input i, late in the copy (recall_idx >= 5)
explanation: Token-specific, position-gated feature. It fires only in the copy phase and only when the fed-back input token is i (100% of activation mass is on in_tok=i). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases. It also never fires on the first occurrence of i, because copy-phase inputs are always repeats. Firing rate on copy-phase i rises steeply with recall position: near zero for recall_idx <= 3, about 0.6% at recall_idx 4, then 3%, 8%, 12% and 14% lift for recall_idx 5 to 8. Activations at recall_idx >= 5 hold about 99% of the mass. Long sequences (L = 8, 9) hold 87% of the mass. The token being output at the same step also modulates firing: rates are highest when it is i, v, s, d, u, w or x, and the top activations are mostly i followed by i or v near the end of the copy. The simple predicate copy & in_tok=i & recall_idx>=5 gets mass recall 0.99 but precision only 0.48 (dev). Adding the out_tok set at recall_idx 5 raises dev F1 to 0.77. Many late copy-phase i steps still do not fire, and no checked variable fully explains those false positives.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: i, d, v, x, -, <DEL>; least: z, a, k, f) and the token being output (most: i, v, s, d, u, w; least: k, z, e, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=7, recall_idx=6, t=15.
